summary: Phase 11.1 complete. Rabinovich Cor 5.4(1)/(2), unanchored and anchored, re-based onto HasFaithfulDedekindINF: four binders swapped at BoundedFixFaithful.lean:204,:277 and BoundedFixAnchoredFaithful.lean:165,:248, with not one proof step changed in any of the four. Phase 11's eight predicted call sites needed NO edit -- each passes h_INF straight through, so the binder change alone fixed them. THE CHARTERED SHIM IS DELETED: coeHasDedekindINFToFaithful and its 33-line section note are gone, Lemma53Faithful.lean 601 -> 565 lines, with no remaining reference anywhere in FormalSystem/ and the full build green without it. CONFIRMED neither module opens the carrier -- h_INF appears only as an argument to negChainOnFaithful_iff, never rcases'd or projected -- so the v8 survey's 'no destructure sites' finding holds and the Phase 11 fallback is not triggered. One real survey miss found and recorded as deviation D3: five transitive call sites one module further down went red and were fixed with an explicit coercion, no statement touched. Full lake build green (1919 jobs), sorry-free, axiom-clean, all three canaries unchanged.

shim_deletion.what_was_removed: The instance (4 lines) plus the entire '## Re-base compatibility shim — ORIGINAL GLUE, and scheduled for removal' section note (32 lines). 36 lines total; Lemma53Faithful.lean 601 -> 565.
evidence: Declaration-inventory diff of Lemma53Faithful.lean against the prior commit shows EXACTLY ONE removal ('instance coeHasDedekindINFToFaithful') and no other inventory change.
Full lake build is green WITHOUT the instance, so no consumer was silently relying on the coercion firing implicitly.
shim_deletion.territory_exception_honored: Lemma53Faithful.lean received this deletion and nothing else. Phase 11's deviation D1 (the additive HasDedekindSUP.last_occ_tp pair in Lemma53FaithfulPast.lean) was left exactly as landed -- not 'cleaned up', per the dispatch instruction.

carrier_not_opened.detail: In all four _iff proofs h_INF occurs ONLY as an argument to negChainOnFaithful_iff. It is never rcases'd, never projected, never written h_INF.first_occ. The grep hits mentioning 'h_INF.first_occ' in these modules are docstring prose DESCRIBING what negChainOnFaithful_iff does internally, not code. Phase 11's inference was right: an opened carrier would have produced a projection error, not a bare application-type mismatch.
carrier_not_opened.consequence: The v8 Faithful-Subtree Survey's 'no destructure sites' finding for these two modules is confirmed by machine. The chartered Phase 11 fallback (re-base onto HasDenseDedekindINF with explicit endpoint branches) is NOT triggered.

measurement_vs_prediction.phase_11_predicted: Exactly eight Application type mismatch errors on the carrier argument at BoundedFixFaithful.lean:215,:227,:281,:290 and BoundedFixAnchoredFaithful.lean:181,:193,:257,:266, and no other error anywhere.
measurement_vs_prediction.held: YES for the two target modules. Both are pure signature swaps; both scoped builds green on the FIRST attempt; zero failed proof attempts; no proof-search tool (lean_multi_attempt, lean_state_search, lean_hammer_premise) invoked at any point in the phase.
measurement_vs_prediction.surprise: The eight sites needed NO textual edit -- they pass h_INF straight through, so swapping the binder fixed all eight at once. What DID need editing was nine argument positions: the four in-territory _of_attained wrappers (which now compose h_INF.toHasDedekindINF.toHasFaithfulDedekindINF) and five out-of-territory transitive consumers (deviation D3).
measurement_vs_prediction.why_the_probe_missed_d3: Phase 11's probe disabled the shim while leaving the four binders IN PLACE. It therefore measured the consumers of negChainOnFaithful_iff, not the transitive consumers of the four Cor 5.4 _iff's. The latter only redden once the binders actually move. This is a genuine blast-radius gap in the survey's counting method, not a Phase 11 execution error.

deviations.kind: chartered-scope expansion, out of declared territory
deviations.what: At each site the argument h_INF became h_INF.toHasFaithfulDedekindINF. All five consume negBoundedLeftFixAnchoredFaithful_iff, whose binder this phase swapped. NOTHING ELSE in either module changed -- not one binder, statement, docstring or proof step. Both modules' own h_INF binders remain HasDedekindINF.
deviations.why_forced: Once the binder moves, these five are red. The full build cannot be green without either editing them or retaining the shim.
deviations.why_not_keep_the_shim: Retaining coeHasDedekindINFToFaithful would have made the tree green with zero out-of-territory edits AND would have violated this phase's own binding checklist item. The charter's stated reason for deletion is that the shim 'would let a later reader pass a needlessly strong carrier without seeing that they had'. An explicit, greppable .toHasFaithfulDedekindINF at each site delivers exactly that visibility; a silent Coe is what the charter forbids. Between violating the deliverable and a five-token expansion that changes no statement, the expansion is the smaller and more honest cost.
deviations.why_not_blocked: No ambiguity to escalate and no settled design reopened. The fix is forced, mechanical, and verified green. Escalating a five-token coercion would have stalled the route for no decision.
deviations.impact_on_phases_12_and_12_1: NONE to their planned work. When they swap their own h_INF binders to HasFaithfulDedekindINF they must REMOVE these five .toHasFaithfulDedekindINF suffixes -- leaving them would be a type error, so the build enforces it and no tracking is needed.

route_critical_findings.finding: ASSUME THE ONE-MODULE-FURTHER CASCADE RECURS. A shim-disabled probe reveals the direct consumers of the declaration being re-based; it does not reveal the transitive consumers that redden only once binders actually move. Before declaring Phase 12 or 12.1 done, grep the tree for consumers of EVERY re-based _iff, not just the sites the probe reddened. This cost 5 extra edits here; at NegFixOne/NegFixList, whose consumers include the VecEANegFixFaithful and NfMultiAnchorBridge chain, it could cost more.

R11 now holds at the Corollary 5.4 layer as well as the carrier and base-layer-consumer levels: four more consumers re-based with ZERO new proof branches and zero failed attempts. Block D continues on the PRIMARY charter.

This does NOT settle negFixOneFaithful_cover (NegFixOneFaithful.lean:422) or negFixListFaithful_iff (NegFixListFaithful.lean:446). Their Case1/Case2/Case3a/b/c shape is not a two-arm shape. Phases 12 and 12.1 must still transcribe Rabinovich's exhaustive case split (Lemma 5.1, PDF p.9) rather than assume it collapses. Evidence transfers as ENCOURAGEMENT, NOT PROOF.
